compensating.why: hop 1 strips null and undefined from both types before they are compared
hop 2 passes the operands in the other order
hop 4 compares the object forms of the two types

ownership_reason: Only the gold computes the greatest subtype (the meet) of the two types and decides on it; hops 1-4 pass the two types along unchanged. The gold's javadoc promises whether the two types are meaningfully comparable with === and !==; for the constructor types of G and of H (H extends G, so x.constructor of a G may be H) the comparison is not determined, yet the variant gold answers no because their meet, the least function type, is empty. The convention that the least function type is the meet of distinct function types, even of functions that are subtypes of each other, is pinned by FunctionType.getGreatestSubtype / supAndInfHelper ('the LEAST_FUNCTION_TYPE type at the bottom of the lattice') and JSTypeTest testFunctionTypeRelationships; the == sibling JSType.testForEquality never decides a comparison of a function with an object (JSTypeTest testTestForEquality; testFunctionType asserts that a function type can be tested for equality with itself). No change of the operands above the gold (stripping null and undefined, swapping, autoboxing) changes their meet; a hop that answers related or function-typed pairs itself replaces the gold's decision for those pairs (recorded as bypasses).
